questions: Is the box being pushed or pulled when it slides away?
What changes when the force switches from a push to a pull?
segments.say: Push and pull. Watch the PUSH label and arrow appear and the box slide away, then the PULL label and arrow appear and the box slide back closer. A push moves something away from you and a pull brings it closer - both are forces. Keep your student notes open at the push and pull definitions for this scene.

questions: Which way does the friction arrow point, and why?
What would happen to the block on a perfectly smooth slope?
segments.say: Friction slows things down. Watch the block slide down the slope while the rough surface rubs against it, and follow the friction arrow pushing back up the slope against the slide. That rubbing force is friction, and it slows the block down. Now try the push, pull and friction questions on the worksheet in pairs.

questions: Which poles are facing each other in this scene?
Why do the magnets snap together instead of pushing apart?
segments.say: Opposite poles attract. Read the N and S labels on each magnet: S faces N here, so watch the second magnet slide across and snap onto the first with a click. Opposite poles attract - a north pole pulls towards a south pole, even before the magnets touch. Check this against the poles and attract definitions in your student notes.

questions: What is different about the poles facing each other this time?
Which metal can you be sure a magnet will pull, and which metals must you test?
segments.say: Watch out: a magnet does not attract every metal. Watch the magnet turn so N faces N and the magnets push each other apart - like poles repel. Then hold on to the warning about metals before you finish by taking the exit ticket on your own - its first question revisits exactly this metal trap.
segments.watchFor: A magnet attracts every kind of metal. Listen and look for it in pair talk and on the exit ticket: Magnets grab some metals so strongly that they feel like they grab all of them. Send them back to scene s4 and to the correct turn: Magnets ignore most things: they only pull iron and a few metals.
